title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Anthropic ships 'Record a Skill' — teach Claude a workflow by screen-recording it (Jul 22)
bullets.summary: A new demonstration-based setup flow in the Claude desktop app: pick 'Record a skill' from the '+' menu, screen-record yourself doing a task while narrating, and Claude turns it into a reusable, rerunnable skill.
bullets.how: Fastest path yet to feed The Construct's new-skills scan and installed-skills registry: repeated B9S/PRAGMA workflows can be minted into governed skills by demonstration instead of hand-authoring prompt files. Route it into the skills-adoption scan.

bullets.title: MCP spec 2026-07-28 is now 6 days out — the breaking stateless rewrite lands final next Tuesday
bullets.summary: The stateless core (no handshake/session id, any request to any instance, OAuth-aligned auth, formal deprecation policy) plus MCP Apps (server-rendered UI) and the Tasks extension (tasks/get, tasks/update, tasks/cancel) become the ratified spec on Jul 28.
bullets.how: Every MCP server The Construct runs is 6 days from a breaking change; close the migration inventory + hardening checklist this week. Tasks maps directly onto our long-running scan jobs. Load-bearing action.

bullets.title: Google ships Gemini 3.6 Flash (Jul 21) — the cheap, high-volume tier gets another refresh
bullets.summary: Google released Gemini 3.6 Flash on Jul 21, continuing the fast/low-cost lane below its Pro reasoning tier and keeping Flash the default in the Gemini app and AI Mode.
bullets.how: Flash is the natural engine for high-volume, low-stakes Construct batch work (bulk classification, first-pass drafts); worth a cost/quality spot-check against our default for the visibility-scan and content-draft jobs, no re-architecture.

bullets.title: Two more enterprise vendors ship hosted MCP servers — Axonius (asset intelligence) and Syncfusion BoldDesk AI 2.0 (support desk), both Jul 21
bullets.summary: Axonius exposed a hosted MCP server so asset/security context flows into any MCP client in plain English; BoldDesk AI 2.0 added a hosted MCP server giving outside AI tools direct access to help-desk workflows without the vendor UI.
bullets.how: Thin direct fit for signage, but both reinforce the 'every SaaS ships an MCP' thesis PRAGMA sells; treat client SaaS tools (support desks especially) as MCP endpoints one Construct agent orchestrates — a 'replace [SaaS tool]' reference architecture for the Pulse wedge.

bullets.title: arXiv — 'Effective Strategies for Asynchronous Software Engineering Agents' formalizes how to run background agents
bullets.summary: The paper studies agents that work asynchronously (fire-and-forget, long-running, revisited later) and lays out strategies for task decomposition, checkpointing, and reconciling results from parallel background runs.
bullets.how: The Construct already runs scheduled/background jobs (this Pulse scan, the Harvard and visibility scans); the async-agent strategies are a checklist for making those runs idempotent and self-reconciling, pairing with the Jul-28 Tasks extension.

praxis_lesson: Anthropic's 'Record a Skill' collapses skill authoring from writing prompt files to demonstrating a task once — route every recorded skill through the same governance the skills-scan already applies (security review, registry entry) so demonstration-minted skills are assets, not loose macros. Meanwhile the Jul-28 stateless MCP rewrite is six days out and vendors keep shipping hosted MCP servers (Axonius, BoldDesk), so finishing the migration + hardening inventory before the spec lands stays the load-bearing action, not the Gemini 3.6 Flash refresh.
